investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so the pods remained stuck for 130–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes (those matching the pod's node affinity/selector). The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" is identical across all three sibling checks, indicating the resource pool was already saturated before any of the three eval pods were submitted. Because no VM slot could be allocated, the agent pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never received an agent identity or VM state, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) received zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/zombie VMs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive, limiting scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes; if those 2 nodes are unavailable or at capacity for any reason, all remote-agent pods fail.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent VMs that were not torn down (e.g., cleanup in withCleanup at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs failed silently), consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so the pods remained stuck for 130–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes (those matching the pod's node affinity/selector). The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" is identical across all three sibling checks, indicating the resource pool was already saturated before any of the three eval pods were submitted. Because no VM slot could be allocated, the agent pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never received an agent identity or VM state, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) received zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
